title: Viewing sessions
prompt: Product analytics wants one row per viewing session. Write `solve(watch_sessions)` so it groups each member's plays into sessions and returns when each session started and ended and how many plays it had.
rules: Go through each `user_id`'s plays in `started_at` order (`watch_id` settles a tie).

A play continues the session if it starts no more than 30 minutes after the previous play's `ended_at`. Exactly 30 minutes still continues it; more starts a new session. A member's first play starts a session.
If the previous play has no `ended_at`, the play continues the session.
Return `user_id`, `session_start` (first `started_at`), `session_end` (latest `ended_at`) and `plays`, one row per session.
hints: Mark each play that starts a session with 1 and the rest with 0, using the gap in seconds from the previous play's end.
A running sum of the marks over the member's plays gives a session number. `F.lag(..., 1, 0)` makes the first play count as a new session.
Group by `user_id` and the session number, then take `F.min("started_at")`, `F.max("ended_at")` and `F.count("*")`. Don't return the session number.
starter:
